title: Sputum test for tuberculosis (microscopy and rapid PCR)
what: This test checks the phlegm you cough up from your lungs. It looks for the tuberculosis germ.
why: For a cough lasting more than two or three weeks, coughing up blood, night sweats, weight loss, after contact with someone with TB, and to check treatment.
duration: collection takes a few minutes; the rapid result usually comes in 1 to 2 days, a culture can take up to several weeks
tell_doctor: How many weeks you have had the cough, and if there is blood in the phlegm
If you had TB before, and how it was treated
If you were in contact with someone who has TB
If you have HIV or diabetes, or take medicines that weaken the immune system

prepare.title: Morning
prepare.text: It is best to collect phlegm in the morning, right after waking up, before eating.

prepare.title: Mouth
prepare.text: Before collecting, brush your teeth and rinse your mouth with boiled water.

prepare.title: Samples
prepare.text: Usually 2 to 3 samples are needed, on different days, or in the morning and later in the day. Your doctor will say how many.

prepare.title: Place
prepare.text: Collect phlegm outdoors or by an open window, away from other people.

steps: Take a sterile container. Open the lid only right before collecting
Take a few deep breaths and hold your breath
Cough hard from deep in your chest
Spit the phlegm into the container. It must be phlegm, not saliva
Close the lid tightly and take it to the lab
feel: If the phlegm will not come up, a warm drink the evening before helps
after: Until you get the result, wear a mask around other people
If the test is positive, your doctor will explain the treatment in detail
red_flags: Coughing up a lot of blood: call emergency services
Severe shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services
A fever that does not go down for several days: see a doctor

faq.q: Can I give saliva if there is no phlegm?
faq.a: No, saliva will not work. Tell the nurse. There are ways to help you cough it up.
Yes. Treatment is long, but if you take your medicines regularly, TB is usually cured.

reminders.text: Sputum collection tomorrow morning. Right after waking, brush your teeth, rinse your mouth, and cough the phlegm into the container.
